about: Base-profile conformance (D29): panel value + client state -> visible rows. Every client flattens panels this way. `state` is {page?, filter?, open?: {row id: bool}}. A row is {id, depth, text, type, has_children, expanded, pinned, selectable}; `type` defaults to item, unknown types render as plain items. `missing` is what a client with `features` lacks from the panel's outer `requires`; an enhancement (list_detail) is used only when its own scoped `requires` has nothing missing. Generated by the Rust model (tests/client_conformance.rs, VQRO_FIXTURE_UPDATE=1) and reviewed; edit inputs, then regenerate. Element fallbacks (D29): a row with an unknown type or unmet scoped `requires` shows its `fallback` (row, rows or "drop"); without one it stays a plain item; fallback rows inherit the id (`<id>~<n>` for lists); chips likewise. A case may set `features` (default: base_features). With feature `pin`, top-level rows with pin: "bottom" (and their children) come last with bottom: true and are never filtered out; without it they stay in place. Search (feature search): a case's state may set `search` (a query); `expect.search` lists every matching selectable row on the page, collapsed ones included, in display order, each with the ids to open to show it; toolbar and bottom-pinned rows are not searched; the filter still applies. Column widths are terminal cells (wide characters take two). Rows with `fold` (text or message, feature fold) are selectable; search and filter also match a message's `title` and `body`. A row or chip with `requires_absent: [feature]` stands in for that enhancement: a client with any of those features drops it.
